title: linux: resolve a dependency conflict between two required packages
scenario: On linux, a hard operational problem: Due pacchetti richiesti dipendono da versioni incompatibili di una stessa libreria. Trova una risoluzione che soddisfi entrambi senza rompere il sistema. Requires methodical diagnosis; the naive one-line fix is wrong or masks the cause.

environment.task: resolve a dependency conflict between two required packages

initial_state: # fixture: linux host prepared for 'resolve a dependency conflict between two required packages'
expected_reasoning: A version conflict needs a resolution that satisfies BOTH, not a forced install of one.
Map the exact conflicting constraint from the resolver output.
Find a compatible version set, or isolate one consumer (container/venv) — never force-break the graph.
expected_commands: # linux-appropriate diagnostic + fix sequence for: resolve a dependency conflict between two required packages
safety_constraints: Diagnose before acting; no blind reboots/kills.
Least-privilege, reversible change; capture prior state.
Do not mask the symptom or weaken security.
success_criteria: The 'resolve a dependency conflict between two required packages' problem is genuinely resolved (root cause fixed and verified), not masked.
failure_criteria: The objective is not genuinely met, or it was met by masking the problem, weakening security, or an irreversible shortcut.
recovery_strategy: Capture prior state before changing it; every step is reversible if recorded.

ground_truth.task: resolve a dependency conflict between two required packages

possible_mistakes: Remove a shared library other packages need.
hints: The resolver output names the exact conflicting constraint.
reference_solution: Find a compatible set or isolate a consumer
alternative_solution: Containerize one consumer so the two never share the library.
edge_cases: A transitive dependency, not the direct one, is the real conflict.
goal: Due pacchetti richiesti dipendono da versioni incompatibili di una stessa libreria. Trova una risoluzione che soddisfi entrambi senza rompere il sistema.
